713.t: When his uncle died and his reputation among musicians
713.s: Nelson places his uncle's death before the war, during the Depression, and Russell says people like George Guesnon call him a wonderful musician.
713.ch: Down in St. Bernard and the uncle
713.q: that was before the war I guess? that was before the war I guess? that was in round and before the war I guess? yeah the depression was on then most mm-hmm

951.t: Remembering a fellow inmate who died in 1959
951.s: A speaker remembers a young inmate who helped the prison and died at Camp A on August 11, 1959, before Oster's expected return; he was 35.

606.t: Charlie Christian's influence and his early death
606.s: Hearing Charlie Christian made Ellis play far fewer notes; Christian changed solo guitar and died at 23, as did bassist Jimmy Blanton at 21.
606.q: Well Charlie Christian, I mean when I first heard him I was just absolutely stunned you know. And I was a kid at that time and I could play a lot of notes, I mean a lot of notes, but they were worthless you know. So when I heard him and it got to me so then I started playing from playing a million…

343.t: The Charles Lloyd group's spirit and Keith Jarrett's illness
343.s: McBee calls the Lloyd group one of his most precious experiences and is moved by news of Keith Jarrett's stroke.
343.q: I almost broke down and cried because I’ve looked forward to play with this guy again, in memory of what we had attained. And so it brought back all of those memories about who we were. And so I say a prayer for him.

396.t: Losing a friend and musicians who died in the pandemic
396.s: She lost a friend from her twelve-step group in March; Rowe recalls Pizzarelli, Longo and Marsalis dying within days.
396.q: No? Oh lost, you mean lost, oh. I did. I lost one friend from my twelve-step group, yeah. He was a healthcare worker and I very much liked him and he was a huge contributor to the program. So yeah, he died, very early on, in March.

491.t: Coltrane's illness and death, and friends lost too early
491.s: Golson regrets Coltrane's early death and those of Clifford Brown and Freddie Hubbard, and worries about Horace Silver; he jokes that he is hanging on.
491.q: Yeah. I really don’t like to get into that. But yeah, he was having problems, which I’m sorry about. I feel that so much was at stake. Why endanger that? He should have still been here. If he’d still been here, he would have been 82. He would still have something to say. I know it. Like so many of…

704.t: Patti Bown and the friends he has lost, from Jimmy Cleveland to Isaac Hayes
704.s: Jones recalls Patti Bown's breakdown, Janet Thurlow's help getting him into Hampton's band, and lists friends who have died, including Jimmy Cleveland, Max Roach and Isaac Hayes, and mentions A Secret Garden being redone.
704.ch: Losses, politics and the country's culture
704.q: I know. Patti Bown, we were trying to get when she was 12 years old. She lived right across from the Washington Social Club, and her mother and father didn’t want her to talk to me, because she was playing with symphonies when – she was a genius. We wanted to play in nightclubs. They didn’t want us…

109.t: Charlie Christian at Minton's, and his final illness
109.s: Late in 1941 Clarke met Charlie Christian, who came to Minton's with Mike Bryan and left his amp there; a nurse friend cared for Charlie at the hospital until he died.
109.ch: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
109.q: And he told him a joke or something, and Charlie laughed so hard that he had a coughing spell. And a nurse who was a very good friend of mine -- and I told her -- I knew she was working there, it was the Seaview, I think it was.

94.t: Red Allen, Buster Bailey and the friends who have died
94.s: Moore reflects on his friendship with Red Allen and Buster Bailey and lists those who died, and the jazz clubs he visited while with Lanin.
94.q: Yes -- I should say at this point that when I was with Lester Lanin I always thought of my nights at the Stuyvesant Casino and the Central Plaza and wondering how the boys are doing and I was quite busy with Lester. But my memory always returned to the different guys I was close to. And the fellas…

97.s: Nineteen members died in 1965; he lists his friends.
97.q: No, no, no, it's beyond me now. I'm too old for that now. Don't you understand? Listen, do you know what I'm saying? Let me tell you this in all sincerity. In the Amsterdam Club, in 1965, 19 of those fellows died. I have played with every one of them in the Amsterdam. I went to 17 funerals, because…

76.s: Ladnier died at Mezz Mezzrow's house with a pad and pencil in hand. Zutty and Buck Washington, who lived in the Singletons' building on 47th Street, went there.
76.q: You know he and (Fletcher?) were living there right where we were living on 47th Street
